flagged.evidence: The Statement says that any two parenthesised reorderings of a finite list are "canonically and uniquely identified" without fixing occurrence labels or an induced permutation. For a repeated factor X, the unlabelled source and target can both be X\otimes X, yet there are two canonical endomorphisms: 1 and c_{X,X}. In the scoped example ex-the-sign-braiding-on-supervector-spaces, for a purely odd one-dimensional X, its displayed formula gives c_{X,X}(v\otimes v)=-v\otimes v, so c_{X,X}\ne1 over a field of characteristic not 2. The cited symmetric-coherence theorem only gives equality for composites with the same underlying permutation; it does not make 1 and the transposition equal after repeated occurrences are forgotten.
